work.title: Da den høysalige Konge, Frederik den Femte, blev samlet med sine Fædre, blev følgende Kantate opført

history.p: Though Scheibe had been pensioned as Kapellmeister in 1748, he was still employed by the court to compose music for many official events such as royal birthdays or wedding celebrations. When Frederik V passed away in 1766, the Lord Chamberlain, Adam Gottlob Moltke, ordered – or requested – Scheibe to take care of the musical aspects concerning the funeral. For that he composed a cantata (SchW B2:415) to be performed at Christiansborgs Slotskirke on 18 March 1766. For the following day, when the king was to be buried in Roskilde Domkirke around thirty kilometres west of Copenhagen, Scheibe composed the present cantata of which only the text has survived. At first sight it seems that this cantata is the same as SchW B2:415; however, collating the texts of the two works reveals that the first two-thirds of the present cantata has a very different text clearly indicating that the music could not have been the same. It is likely that the final third of the work was the same, however.

annot.p: 'Aus diesem schönen Singgedichte, dessen Verf. Herr Joh. Ewald ist, wollen wir unsern Lesern diese Arie zur Probe mittheilen [...] Der Gedanke, daß das Grab ein sicherer Hafen der Ehre sey, ist eben nicht gewöhnlich; aber wie wahr ist er nicht! Und deswegen wird er vermuthlich auch vielen wohlgefallen.'
